title: Pakistan and the Taliban: the border on fire
lines: Pakistan and Afghanistan's Taliban government are locked in a dangerous conflict along their border.
Clashes began on October the twelfth and have flared in several places along the frontier, with each side blaming the other for starting them.
On October the seventeenth, the two sides exchanged fire for nearly four hours, in Kurram district and across the border in Afghanistan's Paktia province.
Pakistani officials said Taliban fighters were killed and border posts destroyed. Afghan media reported Pakistani soldiers killed. Neither claim has been independently verified.
Pakistan accuses the Taliban of sheltering militants, including the Pakistani Taliban, the TTP. Kabul rejects that accusation.
Tensions rose after a suicide attack in north-western Pakistan on September the eighteenth, which killed thirty-one people.
Talks in Moscow on October the fifth ended without a joint statement, after disagreements between Pakistan and the Taliban.
The United Nations mission in Afghanistan counted thirteen civilians killed in cross-border attacks between July and September.
Russia, China and the European Union have all urged dialogue, and China has told the Taliban to act against militant groups.
On October the eleventh, the federal government also imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the PTI-governed province on the border, citing security.
For families on both sides of the frontier, the fighting has brought fear, and some have fled their homes.
